rationale: Enabled the demotion variant now that a recovered apply-side rejection is counted rather than fatal, and the sweep immediately produced the shape @joint_apply_order was asking about, through the repository's own producers. Draft-side the revision runs to completion and reports invalid_change_applies=3 with invalid_change_reasons=["config is already joint","config is already joint","config is already joint"] against 245 configuration changes, 446 restarts, 481 elections, 51 unapplied-conf-change check points, stalled_states=0 and violations=0: a node was handed a committed joint-entering configuration change while its own tracker was joint, three times, inside a single process run of the fixed harness with application lag, configuration events aimed at serving members (demote/promote) as well as the joining node, joint transitions, restarts and the liveness witness. That does not show a safety violation - the four invariants still held - but it does show the panic path is reached by permitted event sequences rather than being excluded by the propose-time guard when the change concerns a member other than the leader's own configuration, which narrows the conclusion I recorded two turns ago. I therefore correct that knowledge entry's premise (the residual case is not limited to DisableConfChangeValidation), keep the safety/source-level half that still holds, and request isolated execution of these bytes so the three occurrences and their reasons are receipt-backed; if the receipt reproduces them, the next step is a deterministic prefix that preserves the entry order at the rejecting node, since the sweep does not record it.

knowledge.statement: Propose-time: stepLeader's MsgProp path computes alreadyPending = pendingConfIndex > raftLog.applied and, unless Config.DisableConfChangeValidation is set, rewrites a proposed conf change to a normal entry for that condition and for the alreadyJoint/wantsLeaveJoint mismatches, evaluated against the leader's own tracker. Apply-side: a joint-entering change applied at a node whose tracker is joint is still rejected with 'config is already joint' - the deterministic case shows the precondition (CheckRun eb27767ba74043ada1911d66fc9c4188 index 16), and the sweep with application lag and configuration events aimed at serving members now records three such rejections inside one run (invalid_change_applies=3 with reasons all 'config is already joint' against 245 configuration changes), with no invariant violation. The two guards are therefore not a complete exclusion of the shape: the propose-time check bounds what the leader may append given its own applied configuration, but a node can still be handed a joint-entering change while its own configuration is joint when the lagging configuration belongs to that node rather than to the leader.
knowledge.conditions: Leader-side check as before. Apply-side observation: sweep revision with application lag (one node's apply skipped about one time in six), single-change ConfChangeV2 proposals half of them JointImplicit, targets drawn from the joining node or an existing non-leader member, restarts, four real state machines in one process.
knowledge.changed_premise: The previous revision concluded that for the default configuration the ordering requirement is enforced at propose time and satisfied at apply time by auto-leave, with the residual case limited to Config.DisableConfChangeValidation=true, and that the earlier harness panic was therefore a harness modelling error rather than a shape reachable through permitted histories. The sweep now reaches the shape with default validation: three apply-side rejections with reason 'config is already joint' in one run while the four invariants held, so the premise that the guards exclude the shape must be narrowed to 'the guards bound what the leader appends given its own applied configuration; they do not exclude a joint-entering change reaching a node whose own configuration is joint'. The remaining unresolved part is the exact entry order at the rejecting node, which the sweep does not record and which a deterministic prefix must preserve.

knowledge.assertion: the campaign admission guard shares the same applied/committed gap that lets a configuration change be committed but unapplied at a node

scope.description: Eleventh revision of the same fixed harness; probes A-C and the deterministic joint-change case are unchanged. The sweep now draws configuration-event targets from the joining node 4 or from an existing non-leader member (so a serving voter can be demoted to a learner and promoted back), keeps application lag (one node's apply skipped about one time in six), keeps single-change ConfChangeV2 proposals half of them JointImplicit, keeps restarts and the liveness witness, and applies each committed conf change under a recover that increments invalid_change_applies and records up to five recovered messages in invalid_change_reasons, both reported by invariant_sweep_summary together with the existing counters.
assumptions: Everything comes from the snapshot's own facilities (newTestRaft, newTestMemoryStorage, newNetwork, nextEnts, confChangeToMsg, applyConfChange, hasUnappliedConfChanges, promotable, newRaft, SetHardState); no production logic is modified.
A recovered applyConfChange rejection is recorded as an occurrence with its message; the instrument does not claim which entry order produced it.
Targets exclude the current leader so that proposals keep flowing; that is a harness choice and is recorded as such.
Randomness is fixed per seed; counts are descriptive, not rates.

experiment.prefix: For each of 60 seeds: build nodes 1..4 with newTestRaft(id,10,1,newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1,2,3))); nt := newNetwork(nodes[1],nodes[2],nodes[3]) then nt.peers[4] = nodes[4]. For 60 steps pick one of MsgHup, MsgProp, tick(), isolate, recover, TransferLeader, a ConfChangeV2 proposal on the leader (single change, target drawn from node 4 or a non-leader member, half the time JointImplicit), a restart of a random node from its persisted hard state and applied ConfState, or persist/apply of all nodes; after each step persist/apply nodes 1..4 (skipping one node about one time in six; applying committed conf changes under recover, counting rejections and capturing up to five messages), then evaluate the four invariants and the liveness witness, finally emitting invariant_sweep_summary with all counters including invalid_change_applies and invalid_change_reasons.
experiment.revision_reason: Same investigation, with the demotion variant of the configuration events enabled now that an apply-side rejection is counted instead of aborting, and with the rejection reasons captured. A draft-side run reported invalid_change_applies=3 with all three reasons 'config is already joint' alongside violations=0, which is construction feedback only and is why isolated execution is requested.
